questions.q: Which three input groups does TFT use?
why: Those are data types, not TFT's groups.

questions.q: Sort: 'promotion planned for next week' belongs to which group?
why: Correct: you know the plan for the horizon.
It is known ahead, not only in the past.

questions.q: Pinball loss, q = 0.9, y = 50, forecast = 40. Loss?
Pinball loss, q = 0.1, y = 50, forecast = 60. Loss?
What do TFT's variable selection weights tell you?
options: How much the model relies on each input feature.
The exact causal effect of each feature.

questions.q: Your TFT's q10-q90 band covers only 55% of the test values. What does this tell you?
options: The band is too narrow: the model is overconfident or the data shifted.
why: Correct: an 80% band should cover about 80%.
A too wide band would cover more than 80%.

questions.q: A data set has 3 months of data for 5 stores. Which plan is best?
options: Start with seasonal naive and a simple boosted-tree model; try TFT only if the data size justifies it.
Train TFT first; it is the best model.
why: Correct: little data favors simple models.
No model is best by default.
